text: Age: 45
Occupation: Analyst - Los Angeles County Department of Public Health
Getro Elize for Palmdale City Council

As a devoted husband, father of two, U.S. Army Veteran and graduate of Howard University, I've dedicated my life to serving others. As Vice Chair of the Palmdale Planning Commission, I have worked to strengthen neighborhoods, expand housing opportunities, and promote responsible economic development that benefits every resident.

Throughout my career, I have partnered with government agencies, nonprofit organizations, businesses, and community leaders to serve vulnerable populations, including veterans, seniors, individuals experiencing homelessness, justice-involved individuals reentering the community, and youth seeking a second chance. I have connected residents with housing, employment, education, healthcare, and behavioral health services, helping individuals and families achieve greater stability and independence.

If elected, I will focus on creating quality jobs, supporting small businesses, increasing housing opportunities, improving public safety, investing in infrastructure, and expanding educational and workforce opportunities for youth and working families. I believe strong communities are built through transparent leadership, fiscal responsibility, and collaboration.

With a lifetime of public service, proven leadership, and a vision for Palmdale's future, Getro Elize is the clear choice to lead our city forward and deliver practical solutions that strengthen our community and improve the quality of life for every resident.

text: Age: 69
Occupation: Business Owner

I'm running for City Council in District 4 because our community deserves leadership that listens, collaborates, and puts people first. My years of volunteer service with non-profits focused on economic development, education, and family support have shown me what transparent, community-driven representation can accomplish. They've also reinforced a core truth: representation must be by the people and for the people.
My priorities reflect the values of our district:

Fiscal Stewardship: I will ensure taxpayer dollars are managed responsibly and transparently. By pursuing common-sense solutions and reducing unnecessary burdens, we can support sustainable growth and expand opportunity.

Community Engagement: A healthy democracy depends on open dialogue. I will create regular opportunities—such as monthly town halls—for residents to share ideas, voice concerns, and help shape local decisions.

Public Safety & Well-Being: Safety is a shared responsibility. I will strengthen partnerships between residents, law enforcement, and city leadership to build trust, accountability, and a welcoming environment for every family.
Infrastructure: Reliable roads and well-maintained public spaces are essential. I will prioritize improvements that support safe travel, accessibility, and long-term development.
Together, we can restore meaningful representation and build a stronger more connected District 4.

text: Age: 43
Occupation: Councilmember
Palmdale is my home. It's where I'm raising my child.

I enlisted into the military right out of high school and served through September 11th and the years that followed. Service taught me something I've carried ever since: show up, do the work, and finish what you start.

Before I ever held office, I was out in our neighborhoods hauling away illegal dumping and painting over graffiti, not because it was my job, but because it needed to be done. As your Councilmember, I turned that work into the city's Community Preservation Program, helping ensure no neighborhood gets left behind.

Working families here are stretched thin. I've fought to hold the line on costs, bring good-paying jobs closer to home, and secure our fair share of transportation and infrastructure funding so Palmdale residents spend less time commuting and more time with their families.
I believe in safe neighborhoods, clean streets, and a city government that listens, responds, and respects the people it serves.
We've made progress, but there is more work to do. I'll keep showing up, doing the work, and fighting for Palmdale.
I respectfully ask for your vote.

text: Age: 69
Occupation: Community Volunteer

I am running for Palmdale's City Council, District 4, because I believe every family deserves to live in a safe, welcoming community with opportunities to succeed. My priorities are improving public safety, fixing and maintaining our streets and infrastructure, revitalizing parks and creating paths to good-paying jobs. Palmdale is built on hard-working families, dedicated teachers, local businesses, and neighbors who care about their communities. I will work with residents, public safety professionals, educators and local organizations that make a real difference in our daily lives. I will advocate for safer streets, better lighting, improved sidewalks, and well-maintained public facilities. I also believe our parks and community spaces should be clean, safe, and inviting places where children can play, families can gather and neighbors connect, support local business and help strength our local economy. Most importantly, I believe good leadership start with listening making myself accessible, transparent and accountable by always putting the needs of our community first. Together we can build a safer, stronger and more vibrant Palmdale where every family has the opportunity to thrive.
